question: A breast lump with a clinically benign appearance and a benign ultrasound result can be safely discharged without biopsy, as two out of three components of triple assessment are reassuring.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is FALSE. Triple assessment is only complete when ALL three components are assessed. Benign findings on two components are not sufficient — a tissue diagnosis (core biopsy preferred over FNAC) is always required to complete the assessment before a definitive decision.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. Triple assessment requires ALL THREE components (clinical, imaging, and pathological/cytological). A 'triple-negative' benign result (all three reassuring) is needed for safe discharge; benign clinical and imaging findings alone do not exclude malignancy.
